messages:
lina: Heads-up — Starlight Health (HIPAA) just signed LOI. They want a reserved GPU pool + predictable autoscale for critical flows. Need throughput sizing, preheat plan, and security Q answers. Key SLOs: p95 < 250ms for chat, baseline 250 qps, short spikes to 1,000 qps (<= 30s). Can someone run numbers and call out reservations vs burst costs? @raja @devon @katie
raja: Got it. Quick Qs: average tokens per chat request (prompt + response)? how much of traffic is chat vs embeddings vs rerank? any max sequence lengths?
lina: Customer says ~70% chat, 25% embeddings, 5% bulk-rerank. Chat avg = prompt 120 tokens, response 220 tokens. Embeddings ~512 tokens input. Max seq for chat ~1024 but rare.
raja: Cool. Back-of-envelope: baseline qps 250. For chat token/s = 250 * (120+220) = 85,000 tokens/s. Embedding token/s = 250 * 0.25 * 512 = 32,000 tokens/s (but embeddings are mostly encode-only so cheaper). Total effective tokens/s ~117,000. Assuming model variant "redwood-v4-13B-quant" with ~3,000 tokens/s effective per GPU under our batching profile, GPUs_needed = ceil(117000/3000) = 39 GPUs. That feels high — we should separate workloads and route embeddings to encoder-optimized instances (x0.4 cost).
raja: Proposal: reserved pool = 12 GPUs for chat-critical (keeps p95 under 250ms on usual batching), plus an encoder fleet of 6 smaller GPUs for embeddings. Autoscale up to 40 GPUs across both pools for spikes, with prewarm/burst credit policy.
devon: Notes on autoscale: set a fast ramp for short spikes (scaleBy=2 every 10s) but cap per-AZ growth to avoid noisy neighbour. Use burst credits to cover 30s 1,000 qps spikes — calibrate burst credit burn vs reserved cost. Also recommend sticky routing so in-flight KV cache benefits aren't lost during scale.
devon: Example autoscale policy snippet (Redwood config):
```yaml
autoscale:
  min_replicas: 3
  reserved_replicas: 12
  max_replicas: 40
  scale_window: 10s
  scale_step: 2
  burst_credit_policy:
    enabled: true
    credit_pool: 6000_token_seconds
    refill_rate: 300_token_seconds_per_s
```
lina: Nice. Can you quantify expected latency at baseline with 12 reserved GPUs? Also customer cares about cold KV cache on failovers.
raja: With 12 GPUs and batching patterns we've seen, median ~80–120ms, p95 ~230–270ms depending on prompt shape. So 12 is right at the edge for p95 SLA; recommend 15 reserved to hit p95 <250ms headroom. For KV cache: preheat plan = run customer traffic replay during preheat window to populate prefix and KV entries; maintain sticky sessions for 60s after scale events.
katie: From security/HIPAA side — two asks: (1) do we support customer-managed KMS (HSM) for model keys and (2) network egress/isolation for PHI. Answer: yes to KMS integration via customer KMS connectors; Private deployment or Dedicated with VPC peering required for strict egress rules. Please log these in the questionnaire: Service handles PHI in memory only; no disk persistence unless enabled; audit logs available for all requests.
oliver: Pricing check — rough monthly numbers: reserved 15 GPUs (mid-tier A100 equiv) ~ $X/month (quote in contract). Burst credits usage for spikes billed separately; if they want lower variable cost we can propose quantized model variant (2–3x token/s per GPU) but we should validate quality. I'll draft two options: (A) 15 reserved + burst credits for spikes, (B) 8 reserved + larger burst pool + higher per-token on-demand spend.
lina: Customer also sent security questionnaire — I'll attach later. @katie can you confirm wording for KMS and retention?
katie: Confirmed. Wording to include in questionnaire: "Data is encrypted at rest and in transit; customer-managed keys supported via KMS; no persistent logging of raw inputs unless explicitly enabled; audit logs retained per contract". Ill add HIPAA appendix.
raja: Ops runbook items: preheat job (replay 5% of peak traffic for 10–15 minutes), KV warmup probe every deploy, automated rollback to smaller model variant if tail latency > 500ms for >2 minutes, telemetry alerts for token/s per GPU and queue depth.
deploy-bot: Scheduled job created: `preheat/starlight-2026-06-08` -> runs 2026-06-08T02:00:00Z, replay 5% of sample traffic.
lina: Perfect. Next steps: @raja draft final sizing note + suggested contract language for reserved pool and burst credits; @oliver produce rough pricing options; @katie finish sec Q responses. I'll sync with customer Wed EOD. Thanks all :rocket:
